confirm.rationale:
The advisory (GHSA-8prr-286p-4w7j / CVE-2026-34400, CWE-89) says the Postgres parser for the ?q= search built WHERE clauses by interpolating user search terms via f-strings. It gives 9.1.0 as the fix, with the parser switching to %(name)s placeholders passed to psycopg2's cursor.execute().

The proposed commit aeba85a37a09 ('Replace mongo-specific query stirng syntax with database agnostic (#712)', 2018-10-18) does not fix this. It creates the vulnerability. In its parent cc0993d, postgres/utils.py raised NotImplementedError("'q' search parameter is not currently supported"). aeba85a replaces that with query = [repr(expression.parseString(params.get('q'))[0])] and qvars = dict(). It also adds postgres/parser.py, whose SearchTerm.__repr__ builds SQL such as '"{}" ILIKE \'%%{}%%\''.format(field, word) straight from user tokens. So the proposed vulnerable commit cc0993d had no q= support at all, and the pair is reversed. The advisory lists PR #712 only as a resource, apparently to show where the parser came from.

The real fix is fdd52cd1abad ('fix(security): parameterize Postgres query parser to prevent SQL injection (#2040)', 2026-03-27, parent 71c098d8). Its commit message matches the advisory text almost word for word. It adds to_sql(params) to SearchModifier, SearchAnd, SearchOr, SearchNot and SearchTerm. Every user value (singleterm, phrase, wildcard, regex, range bounds, attribute key) now goes into a params dict as %(_qp_N)s. QueryParser.parse returns (sql, params). Alerts.from_params and Blackouts.from_params in postgres/utils.py set qvars = dict(parsed_vars), so the values reach cursor.execute as bound parameters.

The parts still interpolated after the fix are limited:
- Field and attr identifiers sit inside double quotes, and the grammar's valid_word excludes the '"' character.
- The one-sided range operator is restricted to >=, >, <=, <.
- One gap remains: the default_field from the q.df parameter is still inserted into the SQL by str.replace in QueryParser.parse. That is the neighbouring q.df parameter, not the q= weakness the advisory describes, and I found no follow-up commit on origin/master that addresses it (the clone's master ends at 2026-03-30).

Completeness: git log --all --grep for the CVE/GHSA ids, 'sql injection' and 'parameteriz' finds only fdd52cd and its PR-branch twin b06f653, which has an identical source diff. Nothing touched queryparser.py after fdd52cd. The only later commits to postgres/utils.py are unrelated (#2049 counters, #2047 self-update allowlist).

Main line: fdd52cd is on origin/master, the earliest tag containing it is v9.1.0 (git describe: v9.1.0~16), and that matches the advisory's patched version 9.1.0.

Verdict: 'wrong' for the proposed commit. The canonical fix is fdd52cd, and the correct vulnerable parent is 71c098d8bb8091e76edaefeef4662eb77c753ce7, not cc0993d.

confirm.rationale:
Advisory: CVE-2016-8640 is a CWE-89 SQL injection affecting pycsw before 2.0.2, 1.10.5 and 1.8.6. It lets an attacker read any table and, on PostgreSQL, change data. The advisory references PR #474 and three commits: 69546e1, 522873e and daaf09b.

Diff (d1a79ec -> 69546e1): at the vulnerable commit, CQL_TEXT constraints were written straight into constraint['where'] with type 'cql' and empty values. The only processing was server.py::_cql_update_queryables_mappings, which just replaces queryable names with DB column names. Repository.query, update and delete then ran that string as `filter(text(constraint['where']))`, so any SQL in the CQL was executed. The fix adds pycsw/ogc/csw/cql.py::cql2fes1, which parses CQL into an OGC fes1 Filter XML tree. It then replaces all four raw-CQL paths (getrecords KVP and _parse_constraint, in both csw2.py and csw3.py) with fes1.parse(). That builds the WHERE clause from validated queryables and bind parameters (:pvalueN), and invalid input produces an exception report. The SRU path sets constraintlanguage=CQL_TEXT, so it is covered as well. The commit also stops echoing DB error text ('Invalid query: %s' becomes 'Invalid query syntax'). This is the right component and the right parameter, and the patch on its own neutralizes the injection.

Main-line check: `git branch -r --contains 69546e1` shows only origin/2.0, and its earliest tag is 2.0.2. The other two advisory commits are also backports: 522873e is only on origin/1.10 (tag 1.10.5) and daaf09b is only on origin/1.8 (tag 1.8.6). The pair.json flag 'no fix commit is on the default branch' is accurate. The main-line change is d83df944b1fc0f266444c31852c7730f0f41db87, with the same subject, author Tom Kralidis, dated 2016-10-09 and parent cd425019. It is the second parent of merge 2565ab3, 'Merge pull request #474 from tomkralidis/cql-sru-query-handling', which is the PR the advisory cites. It is on origin/master and first tagged in 2.2.0 (2018-03-20). Its csw2.py and csw3.py hunks match 69546e1 line for line, and `git diff 69546e1 d83df94 -- pycsw/ogc/csw/cql.py` is empty.

Why 'partial': the verdict options don't fit this case exactly. The proposed commit is a complete, content-identical backport of the fix on the 2.0 maintenance branch, and it is not the main-line change. No extra commits are needed for the security fix, which is why additional_fix_commits is empty. For the dataset, the canonical main-line pair is cd425019eea7809f48609821c68c6afc42bf2dde -> d83df944b1fc0f266444c31852c7730f0f41db87. If a release-branch pair is acceptable, d1a79ec -> 69546e1 is itself a valid vulnerable/fixed pair. first_release_with_fix is 2.0.2 because the fix first shipped in 2.0.2 and 1.10.5 on 2016-10-18 and in 1.8.6 on 2016-10-19. It changes `condition.split()` to `condition.split(None, 2)`, which is a functional fix, not a security fix. Nothing later corrects or completes the injection fix.

- repo.git.ls_remote(url, upload_pack=...) is not guarded, which gives RCE.

confirm.rationale:
Advisory: GHSA-3x47-w4rx-6pm7 / CVE-2024-3429 names `sanitize_path_from_endpoint` and `sanitize_path` in lollms/security.py. It describes arbitrary file read on Windows by bypassing their traversal protection, with first patched version 9.5.0. Both the OSV references and the GitHub advisory API (gh api advisories/GHSA-3x47-w4rx-6pm7) cite commit f4424cfc3d6dfb3ad5ac17dd46801efe784933e9 directly.

Vulnerable code (5f406b9): both functions reject a path when the regex `(\.\.+)|(/+/)` matches or when `Path(path).is_absolute()` is true, and only then call `path.lstrip('/')`. On Windows a string such as "/C:/Windows/win.ini" has no drive, so pathlib does not treat it as absolute, and it contains no ".." or "//", so it passes both checks. lstrip then turns it into "C:/Windows/win.ini", a real absolute path. Endpoints such as serve_user_infos join it onto a base directory (the join discards the base) and pass the result to FileResponse. Some callers also ignore the return value and use the raw input, for example lollms_discussion.py and lollms_binding_infos.py:130.

The fix adds `if path.strip().startswith("/"): raise HTTPException(400)` to both functions (in sanitize_path only when allow_absolute_path is False). This runs before the absolute-path check and before lstrip, so the leading-slash bypass is rejected. That matches the two functions the advisory names and the Windows-specific impact it describes.

The huntr page (db57c343) could not be read (it rendered only the site shell), so I could not confirm whether huntr credits a specific fix commit. That, plus the advisory listing no patched version, is why confidence is medium.

It says add_rag_database, toggle_mount_rag_database and vectorize_folder in lollms_file_system.py do not call sanitize_path_from_endpoint or sanitize_path, which lets an attacker run vectorize operations on .sqlite files in arbitrary directories. The repo was later renamed lollms_legacy, and the same SHA is in this clone.

The diff (28ee567 -> aeace796, one file, +2/-2) swaps the unused import sanitize_path_from_endpoint for sanitize_path. In vectorize_folder it changes `folder_path = parts[1]` to `folder_path = sanitize_path(parts[1], True)`. At the fix commit, sanitize_path (lollms/security.py) rejects `..` sequences, `//`, `$(...)` and shell punctuation by raising HTTPException. The exception is raised inside the worker thread, so the thread dies before VectorDatabase(...) or glob run.

Right component: at the vulnerable commit, vectorize_folder is the only one of the three named functions that takes a filesystem path from the HTTP request.
- add_rag_database gets its folder from a server-side tkinter askdirectory dialog.
- toggle_mount_rag_database takes only database_name, which has to exactly match an entry already in config.rag_databases (find_rag_database_by_name), and the path comes from config.
The fix therefore targets the request-reachable sink and adds the exact measure the advisory says is missing.

Caveats, which argue for medium rather than high confidence:
- allow_absolute_path=True, so an absolute folder path is still accepted. This looks deliberate, because the feature takes user-chosen local folders.
- db_name (parts[0]) is not sanitized before `Path(folder_path)/f"{db_name}.sqlite"`.
- In the non-"::" branch, folder_path = db_path is still unsanitized, although that branch needs someone at the server to answer a GUI prompt.

Checks that pass:

- Its subject is "added sanitization to vectorize_folder paths", and it changes only lollms/server/endpoints/lollms_file_system.py.

confirm.rationale:
Advisory (GHSA-8mrm-r7h3-c3hj / CVE-2024-6281): path traversal in apply_settings of lollms before 9.5.1. It says sanitize_path "does not adequately secure the discussion_db_name parameter". The advisory lists this exact commit (parisneo/lollms 26a3ff3) as its fix, and GitHub's first_patched_version is 9.5.1.

What the bug was: at the vulnerable commit 473ae0a, apply_settings builds a list called path_traversal_prone_settings and applies sanitize_path(config[key]) to every key in it. In that list, "discussion_db_name" had no trailing comma before "user_avatar". Python joins adjacent string literals, so the list held one entry, "discussion_db_nameuser_avatar", and never "discussion_db_name". The discussion_db_name value from the request JSON therefore went into lollmsElfServer.config unsanitized and was saved.

Where it lands: the config value is consumed as a path component in lollms/app.py::build_long_term_skills_memory (personal_discussions_path/discussion_db_name, then mkdir(parents=True), then skills_memory.json). A value like ../../x lets an attacker create or write folders outside the discussions directory. This matches "write to important system folders".

What the fix does: the one-character diff adds the missing comma. discussion_db_name becomes a real list member, so sanitize_path (which rejects '..', leading '/', absolute paths and '$()') now runs on it. That neutralizes the described weakness in the right component and for the right parameter.

Why nothing else is needed:
- The neighbouring endpoints were already safe at the vulnerable commit. update_setting runs sanitize_path on setting_value, and select_database runs sanitize_path on data.name.
- The later history of this file and security.py covers other issues, not this one: 328b960 (SVG sanitization), 4c3c611 (authentication on get_config and other endpoints), 28ee567 and 7292acd (Windows absolute paths and allow_current_folder in sanitize_path). None of them touch discussion_db_name.
